instructions: Stir the 1/4 cup sugar and the 1/2 tsp cinnamon together in a shallow dish. Line a plate with paper towels and fit a piping bag with a large open star tip.
Pour the oil into a heavy pot until it's about 2 inches deep and set it over medium heat to warm up while you make the dough.
In a medium saucepan, put 1/4 cup water, the 1/4 cup milk, 4 tbsp of the butter, the 1/2 tsp sugar and the pinch of salt. Bring it to a boil over medium heat, stirring, until the butter has melted.
Take the pan off the heat and add the 1/2 cup flour all at once. Stir hard with a wooden spoon until there's no dry flour left.
Put the pan back over medium low and keep stirring for 2 minutes. The dough will pull into a smooth ball and leave a thin film on the bottom of the pan.
Scrape the dough into a mixing bowl and beat it with a hand mixer on medium for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's stopped steaming.
Add the 2 eggs one at a time, beating until each one is completely mixed in before the next. The dough should be smooth and glossy and fall from the beaters in a thick ribbon.
Spoon the dough into the piping bag.

You're heating the oil to 370°F, so if you have a thermometer, clip it to the side of the pot. No thermometer? Pipe in a small blob of dough: it should sizzle right away, float up and turn golden in about a minute.
Pipe 6 inch lengths of dough straight into the oil, snipping each one off with scissors. Fry 4 or 5 at a time so there's room between them. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Fry them for about 1 1/2 minutes, until the underside is golden brown. Turn them with tongs and fry the other side for another 1 1/2 minutes.
Lift them onto the paper towels for 30 seconds, then roll them in the cinnamon sugar while they're still warm. Fry the rest of the dough the same way, keeping the oil between 350°F and 370°F.
method_notes: Both versions cook a choux style dough of water, butter, sugar, salt and flour on the stove, beat in eggs, pipe it through a large star tip into hot oil and roll the churros in cinnamon sugar. Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) adds milk and more butter for a richer dough, fries at 350 to 370°F and flips them halfway. Jo Cooks uses water only, less butter and more sugar in the dough, fries at 375°F and serves them with a dark chocolate dipping sauce, left out here. This one is Natasha's recipe halved for four.
